en.general: A goal state involving the maintenance of human (and other organisms') well-being, needs, and values into the future, together with the durability of a given state over time under perturbation. Sustainability has two connotations that are conceptually distinct: a goal state (what should be maintained, a question of human values) and durability/resilience (how well a state persists, a question science can address) — not all resilient states are desirable, and not all desirable states are resilient (Waring et al. 2015).

examples: Evaluating a climate policy not only by whether the resulting ecological state would persist (resilience) but by whether it actually serves human needs and values (the goal-state question).

The UN Sustainable Development Goals as one attempt to specify what humans collectively need, value, and therefore want to sustain — while recognizing communities may value different things or things not captured by the SDGs.
